## MHA PLACES
Write each new place as somewhere people live and work in present-day Japan, not a backdrop.
- Function and owner: what it is for and who runs it (U.A. faculty, an agency's pro, a shop owner, the city, the police, a villain crew).
- Daily rhythm: morning, afternoon and night (commuter rush, lunch crowd, patrol shifts, a bar that wakes after dark), matched to the current time.
- Access and authority: who may enter (student or faculty ID, visitor pass, license, invitation), who keeps order inside, and what happens to trespassers or illegal Quirk use.
- Repeatable play: what a character can come back to do: train, study, work, shop, eat, rest, recover, investigate, meet someone.
- Japan-specific detail: stations, konbini, vending machines, shrines, apartment blocks, police boxes, hero billboards, agency merch shops, heteromorph-friendly doors and seating.
- One ordinary friction among the people who use it (budget, noise, rankings, turf).

## U.A. ACADEMY
U.A. reads as a modern academy campus behind the U.A. Barrier: the glass main building, homerooms, the Faculty Office, the Development Studio, the cafeteria, gyms, training grounds and Heights Alliance. Students wear uniforms, attend homeroom and live in the dorms. Training spaces show supervision: observation posts, faculty on hand, safety equipment. Use the exact authored location and area names, and never add a campus building that duplicates one.

## OFF CAMPUS
- Hero agencies: a front desk, patrol maps, a briefing room, sidekicks and office staff, a merch shelf.
- Police: stations, police boxes, detectives, holding cells; heroes capture, police process.
- Hospitals: wards, visiting hours, paperwork.
- Villain spaces: ordinary buildings used for crime (a dive bar, a rented warehouse room, a back office), where exits and lookouts matter more than decor.
- Neighborhoods: people going about their day; trouble disrupts ordinary life and never replaces it.

## RULES
- Describe the place as it stands now: damage and added security from events that have happened stay; events that have not happened leave no trace and are never foreshadowed.
- The visible description holds only what anyone could see or learn. Hidden owners, concealed entrances and criminal use go in hiddenInfo; secrets kept in narrator-only notes go nowhere.
- Areas are parts of one place; never turn a hallway, vehicle or waiting room into a new location.
- Generated occupants are ordinary people with jobs; canon characters appear only where their records, schedules or the story place them.

## MHA AREAS FOR NEW PLACES
A new place gets three to six areas named plainly in English, the way authored ones are (Front Desk, Ready Room, Patrol Garage, Station Concourse, Back Alleys), each with paths to its neighbors and one line on who is there and what happens there. Common shapes:
- Small hero agency: Front Desk, Dispatch Room, Briefing Room, Ready Room, Garage; a wall map with pins, a merch shelf by the door, the pro's office upstairs.
- Police box: Counter, Back Office, Holding Bench; a bicycle out front, a lost-and-found shelf, a hand-drawn map of the blocks.
- Convenience store: Counter, Aisles, Magazine Rack by the window, Stockroom, Parking Lot; open all night, a hero-goods display at the end of an aisle.
- Ramen shop or izakaya: Counter, Tables or Tatami Room, Kitchen, Back Door; a ticket machine at the ramen counter, regulars who know the owner.
- Apartment building: Entrance and Mailboxes, Stairwell, Hallway, the apartment itself, Roof.
- Station: Ticket Gates, Platforms, Concourse, exits by direction, Bus Terminal.
- Hospital ward: Reception, Ward Corridor, Patient Room, Waiting Room, Nurses' Station; visiting hours, and an officer at the door of a suspect's room.
- Warehouse or back office used for crime: Loading Bay, Main Floor, Office, Back Exit, Lookout Point.
- Support company workshop: Showroom, Fitting Room, Workshop Floor, Test Bay.
- Shrine: Torii Gate, Approach, Main Hall, Steps; festival stalls in season.
- Also, when the story calls for them: a public bath, a karaoke box, a family restaurant, a game center, a gym or a dojo with shoe lockers at the entrance.

## HIDDEN INFO FOR A PLACE
Who really owns it and who pays for it; who watches it (cameras, the nearest police box, a pro's patrol route, a lookout); its weak points (back exits, roof access, blind spots, delivery hours); any illegal business that uses it and who knows; and one thing that could go wrong there. All of it ordinary and local: no hidden base of a canon group, and nothing a narrator-only note keeps secret.

## SEASON AND HOUR
The year opens in April: falling cherry blossoms, new employees in fresh suits, spring rain. June brings the rainy season; summer brings heat, cicadas, festivals and fireworks; the school terms and exams set the campus rhythm. Describe a place in the current season and at the current hour: shutters down at dawn, a lunch line at noon, neon and patrols at night.

## WHO IS THERE
A place lists the kinds of people found there by role and hour (a counter clerk on the night shift, two regulars at the bar, the owner in the back). Name only those the story will meet, each a distinct individual; a canon character appears only where their record or the story places them.
